checks.summary: For a public repository that publishes a root GitHub Action, link its exact Marketplace listing from the root README.
Keep GitHub auto-merge equal to the effective github.allow_auto_merge policy; an unmanaged setting is left alone.
Build every detected binary, site bundle, napi-rs addon, and Tauri application in GitHub Actions; run full Tauri builds on a scheduled workflow.
Allow and automate pull-request branch updates when strict checks require freshness.
Require pull requests and block force pushes and deletion on the default branch.
Run every declared build, build:* or *:build package target on push or pull requests; Tauri projects also need a change-triggered compile check and a scheduled full build.
Keep a root CHANGELOG.md, CHANGELOG, CHANGELOG.txt, CHANGES.md, or HISTORY.md; format and versioning style are repository choices.
Do not let jobs or gating test, lint, format, typecheck, and build steps hide failures with continue-on-error.
Keep a push or pull-request workflow with test, lint, and format tasks for every detected language; exempt scratch project paths explicitly with ci_exists.ignore.
Keep latest default-branch runs green for active repository-owned workflows.
Give every push and pull-request CI job an explicit finite timeout; reusable-workflow jobs are exempt because GitHub does not allow the setting there.
Let every pull-request matrix job short-circuit: scope the workflow with path filters, condition the job, or expand the matrix from a fanout job that inspects the change.
Run validation on a schedule when periodic coverage should expose repository bitrot between changes.
Gate heavy pull-request jobs with workflow path filters, a job condition, or a dependency on an output-producing fanout job.
Declare each committed generator under [[codegen]] with its project root, command, and output patterns; run it in CI and follow it in the same job with git diff --exit-code or git diff --quiet.
Keep a valid CODEOWNERS file in .github/CODEOWNERS, CODEOWNERS, or docs/CODEOWNERS, in GitHub precedence order, with at least one rule that assigns an @account, @organization/team, or email owner.
Run Codespell from a push or pull-request workflow using its command or registered GitHub Action.

Enforce Conventional Commits in a pull-request or push workflow with a recognized semantic-title action, commitlint, cocogitto, convco, or an explicit failing PR-title validator; mention Conventional Commits in the root README or CONTRIBUTING.md.

Keep a valid .github/dependabot.yml version 2 configuration with a scheduled update covering every detected package ecosystem at its owning directory and GitHub Actions at the repository root; directory globs may be used explicitly.
When github.allow_auto_merge is explicitly enabled, use a Dependabot-only pull-request workflow that fetches update metadata, excludes major updates, and enables auto-merge behind required checks.
At the start of work, find and read `field_guide.md`; append concise, durable discoveries that will help future agents. Keep the file in the repository, preferably at `notes/field_guide.md`.
Commit the repository's Git hooks under .githooks, keep every hook file executable, and have the development script point core.hooksPath at it; a declared hook manager installs itself instead.
Ignore each ecosystem's build junk at every package scope: Cargo requires target/ and Bun, npm, pnpm, and Yarn require node_modules/; applicable ancestor .gitignore files may provide the rule.
In Rust repositories, run Astral's hawk (cargo hawk) from a push or pull-request workflow to flag unnecessarily public APIs.
Keep a root LICENSE, LICENSE.md, LICENSE.txt, COPYING, or UNLICENSE file; GitHub SPDX classification is useful but nonstandard license text is allowed.
Commit the correct lockfile for every detected package ecosystem.
Reference third-party GitHub Actions by commit SHA; local actions are exempt and first-party release channels are allowed.
Use exact npm/Bun dependency versions; local dependencies are exempt and Cargo ranges stay advisory because Cargo.lock owns resolution.
Keep supported project boundaries and manifests detectable by Ordnung.
Keep a root README that opens with an H1 title in its first ten nonblank lines.
Keep the root README between 150 and 1,500 words with install/getting-started, usage/docs, contributing, and license sections, and no broken repository-relative Markdown links.
Keep repository description and issue tracking configured.
Keep GitHub setup-action toolchain inputs off unbounded latest and wildcard versions; explicit versions and bounded stable channels are allowed.
Require every check posted by pull-request workflows before default-branch changes merge.
Declare every package the effective policy requires for a project's language or ecosystem; a workspace member may inherit the declaration from its workspace root.
Give every active branch ruleset that gates merging at least one explicit bypass actor for emergency administration.

Keep detected shell scripts under the configured scripts.directory, except exact scripts.allow paths; provide the configured development script there and name its repository-relative path in the root README.
Keep secret scanning and push protection enabled where available.
When the repository carries shell scripts, run ShellCheck over them from a push or pull-request workflow using its command or a registered GitHub Action.
Keep open pull requests active within 30 days, remove branches already merged into the default branch, and enable automatic branch deletion after merge.
Keep root Markdown and text files conventional or explicitly listed in stray_files.allow; keep working notes under stray_files.notes.
Require status checks to run against the latest default-branch state.
For each package containing CSS, SCSS, Sass, or Less, keep a Stylelint configuration in that package or an ancestor and run Stylelint on pushes or pull requests.
Keep tests out of source files; move an inline test module under the configured test root.
Give every source file a mirrored test file under the configured test root, matching its path and a configured test suffix.
Do not configure test commands or standard Rust and TypeScript test-runner configuration to rerun failures until they pass.
Keep JavaScript and TypeScript projects on an explicit type layer and run their typechecker on push or pull requests.
Keep a root .vale.ini with an existing relative StylesPath when declared, and run Vale from a push or pull-request workflow.
Keep the repository's GitHub homepage setting pointed at its reachable HTTP(S) website.
Keep the repository's default GITHUB_TOKEN read-only and prevent workflows from approving pull requests; jobs that need write access must grant it explicitly with a permissions block.
Run zizmor static analysis over the repository's GitHub Actions workflows from a push or pull-request workflow, using its command or the zizmor-action.
